summary: Sustained 5xx elevation: KV compaction during background snapshot causing upstream GPU memory spike and API 5xxs
description:
Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-12 12:18 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses across several API routes (chat generation and embeddings). Error rates peaked at ~12% error-rate for a 20-minute window for affected tenants.
Impact: Multiple enterprise tenants (notably Acme Analytics) reported timeouts and 502/503 responses for production traffic. Some streaming connections were abruptly reset.
Environment: prod/us-east primary, with spillover observed in eu-west.
Observed pattern: background KV compaction (snapshot/compact job) coincided with a surge in GPU memory usage on a subset of serving runtimes. The serving runtime hit NVML OOM/watchdog resets leading to upstream process crash and 5xx propagation at the API gateway.
Steps to reproduce (observed): 1) Trigger background kv shard compaction during sustained batching workload (high-throughput small-payload chat/embeddings mix). 2) Runtime shows sudden RSS/GPU memory rise within 30-60s of compaction start. 3) Kernel selector triggers a quant fallback path and increased KV cache pressure. 4) NVML watchdog resets GPU process -> upstream runtime exits -> API gateway returns 502/503.
Metrics & logs: - GPU memory high-water marks from /metrics: jump from 60% to >98% on node host-rt-12 within 45s of compaction start. - Runtime logs: "nvml: device reset" and subsequent "watchdog: runtime terminated with signal 6". - APIGW logs: 502 spikes with backend error code "upstream_unavailable" and increased latency preceding errors.
Hypothesis: The compaction job reads KV shards in a way that temporarily increases active KV working set and triggers a path in the runtime that allocates extra GPU-side caches for compaction-related prefetches. Under high batching this pushes device memory over threshold and triggers watchdog. Secondary factor: host-level ephemeral fragmentation (multiple tenants pinned to same GPU pool) reduces available headroom.
Current impact: P1 affecting enterprise tenants with degraded throughput, automated failovers triggered causing increased latency and retried requests.
Next steps taken: 1) SRE throttled background compaction jobs cluster-wide and scaled down compaction concurrency at 12:40 UTC. 2) Temporarily disabled cross-tenant co-located compaction on dedicated GPU pools for enterprise tenants at 12:45 UTC. 3) Tuned runtime to reduce prefetch/concurrent-kv-read window for compaction path (hotfix config).
Workaround for customers: For enterprise tenants affected, we recommended pinning to dedicated pool or lowering concurrency on large-embedding/parallel-chat uploads until fix is rolled out.
Follow-ups: deeper root cause investigation on compaction access pattern, kernel selector unit tests, quantify safe headroom per GPU for concurrent compaction + serving.
comments: 2026-03-12 12:30 UTC - Support (Arielle): Initial alert from monitoring; opened ticket after Acme Analytics reported 502s on production chat route. Attached sample request ids: rq_9901, rq_9902.

2026-03-12 12:38 UTC - SRE (Samir): Observed NVML device reset on host-rt-12 and host-rt-15 coincident with compaction start timestamps. Increasing GPU mem usage recorded. Marking as Sev1 and throttling compaction.

2026-03-12 12:41 UTC - Eng (Marta Li): Looked at kernel selector logs; compaction triggers quant fallback for read path on affected model variant; created a short-lived config to reduce fallback aggressiveness. Rolling config to limited batch of hosts.

2026-03-12 12:50 UTC - Support (Arielle -> Customer): Notified Acme Analytics about ongoing investigation and recommended temporary rate-limiting of burst uploads and pinning to dedicated pool. Customer acknowledged and applied temporary throttling.
2026-03-12 13:05 UTC - SRE (Samir): After compaction throttles and runtime config change error-rate dropped to ~1.2%. Some residual retries observed as edge caches flush. Continuing monitoring.

2026-03-13 09:22 UTC - Eng (Marta): Added unit test cases to exercise compaction read-window and kernel-selection path. Draft PR submitted for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4387.
2026-03-13 12:00 UTC - SRE (Samir): Scheduled controlled canary for compaction concurrency bump in eu-west with additional telemetry; will only proceed if GPU headroom > 30% in target hosts.
2026-03-13 14:30 UTC - Support (Arielle): Notified customer that a configuration workaround and throttles remain in place; customer confirmed improved SLA metrics and asked for postmortem timeline.
investigation_notes: Checked NVML logs and host metrics — resets align with compaction start times across multiple hosts.
Heap/profile analysis shows increased peak GPU allocations from prefetch_kv_reader when compaction reads many small keys; allocation pattern not deallocated promptly.
Kernel selector log indicates fallback to a quant path that uses additional temporary device-side buffers for reordering.
Multi-tenant co-location amplified impact; single-tenant dedicated pools show better resilience to same compaction load.
Related to PR 4387 which introduces safeguards for compaction read windows (draft), needs additional integration tests before rollout.
Plan: add compaction concurrency limiter, adjust kernel-selection threshold for compaction reads, instrument per-tenant compaction headroom metrics.
Possible long-term: move compaction to non-GPU worker or a lower-priority throttle to avoid interfering with live serving.
resolution_notes: Mitigation in place (2026-03-12 12:45 UTC): throttled compaction and applied temporary runtime config to reduce prefetch window — immediate error-rate reduction observed.

Follow-up action items assigned to Eng/SRE: implement compaction concurrency limiter, expand unit/integration tests for kernel selection with compaction, add dashboard for compaction-vs-serving headroom.
Customer follow-up: postmortem and timeline for fixes to be provided by 2026-03-20.
Pending: complete PR review and staged rollout of kernel-selection fix; produce postmortem with root cause and preventative safeguards.
Ticket will be closed once PRs merged and canary run completed with no regression for 48 hours.
